key_insight: Decoder-only LLMs are modeled as a unified multi-index hybrid system spanning layerwise computation, token-level stochastic dynamics, and mode switching for tool use.
engineering_relevance: This framework provides a control-theoretic basis for analyzing and designing agentic LLM systems with more precise reasoning about memory, timing, and external tool interaction.
method: Treat transformer depth as an ultrafast feedforward cascade with layer normalization as spherical projection and KV caching as an exact state realization.
Model token generation as a finite-context Markov chain with stochastic difference recursion over decoding steps.
Represent tool use as a hybrid switching process with trigger manifolds, state jumps, and context augmentation by external observations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports formal theoretical results and bounded error-growth guarantees for prompt-dependent evaluable claims, rather than empirical benchmark evaluation.
watch_item: The framework relies on assumptions such as finite-context truncation, conditional hazard bounds, and idealized switching/jump maps, which may be difficult to validate in real deployed systems.
paper_title: On the Multi-Index, Multi-Rate, and Multi-Phase Dynamics of Decoder-Only Language Models: A Unified Hybrid Framework for Generative and Agentic Systems
